title: Tests with a fixed time limit fail on a loaded machine
what: 12 cores; 20 test files hold a timeout of 10 s or more (grep, 28 Oct). Find the cause, not one example (principle 6): list every test that runs a subprocess or a step with a fixed wall-clock limit; for each, make the test independent of machine speed (an injected clock or budget, or a limit derived from the work) or move it where load cannot reach it. Measure what drives load to 27 (gate slots x test jobs x lanes' own test runs) and whether the gate's job count or slot count should depend on the machine's free capacity.
why: 28 Oct, the second time in one day: tests/test_rules_gate_isolation.py:22 hit its 200 s subprocess timeout in the stub-guard branch's gate (4 test jobs, 1277 s, load average 27), and passed alone in 55 s; earlier tests/test_precheck.py's 3 s budget failed the same way (fixed separately). Neither test was in the changes they turned red. Each red gate of this kind costs a gate fixer and a gate rerun (about 20-25 min) and stops a lane.
failing_case: Run the full gate while another gate and 4 agents run their tests: tests/test_rules_gate_isolation.py fails at its 200 s timeout though it passes alone in 55 s.
pass_cases: The same load: the gate is green 20 times in a row on those tests.
A test that really hangs still fails, by a limit tied to the work, not to the clock of a busy machine.
